title: Regulatory Frameworks — EU, US, UK, Korea

questions.question: Which milestone does the local TIMELINE place first after the EU AI Act entered into force?
options: All transparency duties on the entry-into-force date
High-risk obligations in January 2024 before the Act existed
1 August 2024 entry into force, followed by prohibited-practice and AI-literacy obligations on 2 February 2025
Full applicability in August 2025 with no staged dates
questions.explanation: The code lists entry into force at 2024-08-01 and the first application milestone at 2025-02-02. The staggered schedule is why a compliance map must identify the obligation class, not just one Act date.

questions.question: What is the highest EU AI Act penalty tier stated in the lesson?
options: 15M EUR or 3% for all violations
An uncapped fine with no statutory percentage
7.5M EUR or 1% for prohibited practices
35M EUR or 7% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher, for prohibited practices
questions.explanation: Article 99(3) is the highest tier described: prohibited Article 5 practices can trigger 35M EUR or 7% of worldwide turnover, whichever is higher. Other tiers are lower and tied to different conduct.

questions.question: Which three chapters does the 10 July 2025 GPAI Code of Practice contain?
options: Transparency, Copyright, and Safety and Security
Privacy, bias, and watermarking
Capability, control, and compliance
Training, inference, and deployment
questions.explanation: The local timeline and lesson identify the three chapters and 12 commitments. Transparency and Copyright cover all GPAI providers, while Safety and Security is aimed at systemic-risk providers.

questions.question: What scope change does the February 2025 UK AISI rebrand signal?
options: A merger into the EU AI Office
A narrower focus on frontier-capability security rather than the earlier broad bias and free-speech framing
A complete end to frontier-model evaluations
A new mandate for open-source model weights
questions.explanation: The lesson describes the move from AI Safety Institute to AI Security Institute as a narrower frontier-security remit. It did not remove the Inspect evaluation tool or turn the body into an EU regulator.

questions.question: What policy direction does the June 2025 US AISI-to-CAISI rebrand represent in the lesson?
options: A merger with the FDA
An immediate federal open-weights mandate
A shift toward pro-growth standards and innovation support, with less emphasis on mandatory pre-deployment evaluation
A stricter nationwide pre-market approval regime
questions.explanation: The lesson interprets CAISI as Center for AI Standards and Innovation and links it to a pro-growth policy direction. State rules and sectoral obligations still matter, so the federal shift is not a global exemption.

questions.question: What does the Korean AI Framework Act milestone in the local timeline require of foreign providers?
options: Majority Korean ownership of every model company
No requirements until the EU AI Act applies
Open release of every model weight
A local representative plus risk assessment and safety measures for high-impact or generative AI contexts
questions.explanation: The lesson describes Article 12 and the effective-January-2026 framework as requiring local representation and risk/safety measures. It is not a word-for-word EU Act copy and does not impose a universal open-weights rule.
